Título: The role of tactical police medics in the prehospital environment: results from an interview study.
Contexto: Sweden; national tactical police unit and civilian prehospital-healthcare interface
População: 13 tactical police medics interviewed using a semi-structured protocol
Desenho: qualitative interview study with thematic analysis following Braun and Clarke
Resumo appraisal: AI-assisted provisional JBI appraisal: clear qualitative question, sampling, verbatim transcription, thematic analysis, ethics and participant-derived findings; reflexivity and transferability remain limited.
Extração: Thirteen Swedish tactical police medics described general satisfaction with training but a mismatch between trained competencies and tasks actually performed, legal/medical restrictions on treating third parties, and inconsistent collaboration with civilian prehospital services.
Resultado: The study reports medics' perceptions and experiences; it does not quantify patient outcomes or compare alternative tactical-medical systems.
Supported claims: Interviewed Swedish tactical police medics reported a perceived mismatch between training and operational use and described barriers in the interface with civilian healthcare.
Unsupported claims: The interviews do not establish that expanding police-medic scope improves survival, safety, response time or clinical outcomes.
Limites de transferibilidade: Swedish medical regulation, police organization, tactical-medic training and EMS governance differ from Brazilian public-safety and SUS/SAMU structures.

Título: Family-centered preventive intervention for military families: implications for implementation science.
Contexto: United States Navy/Marine Corps installations; military-family preventive service implementation
População: FOCUS service program expanded from 7 installations in 2008 to 14 by 2010; article reports service reach and initial program outcomes
Desenho: descriptive implementation/program-development report with uncontrolled service-evaluation observations
Versão instrumento: JBI critical appraisal tools; textual evidence route
Resumo appraisal: AI-assisted provisional textual-evidence appraisal: implementation chronology, program architecture and contextual lessons are transparent; early outcome observations are uncontrolled and cannot establish intervention efficacy.
Extração: FOCUS was rapidly adapted and disseminated across military installations, using embedded staff, training, standardized assessment, modular services and quality-improvement feedback. The report explicitly notes development without a prior randomized trial.
Resultado: The paper supports implementation-process lessons and descriptive early observations, not causal effectiveness.
Localização exata: Abstract; Chronology of Intervention Development; Intervention Implementation; discussion of trialability/observability
Supported claims: FOCUS was developed and scaled across multiple U.S. military installations with an implementation model emphasizing embedded staff, standardized training, assessment feedback and adaptable service intensity.
Unsupported claims: This report alone does not prove that FOCUS caused mental-health improvement, is superior to alternatives, or would work similarly in Brazilian security organizations.
Limites de transferibilidade: U.S. military family-service infrastructure, funding, command structure and clinical support differ materially from Brazilian public-safety agencies.

Título: A hybrid type I trial to increase Veterans' access to insomnia care: study protocol for a randomized controlled trial.
Contexto: United States; one large urban Veterans Affairs Medical Center
População: Planned 56 Veterans randomized 1:1 (28 BBTI, 28 CBTI); qualitative implementation samples planned for Veterans, primary-care providers and nurses
Desenho: hybrid type I randomized non-inferiority trial protocol plus CFIR-guided qualitative needs assessment
Resumo appraisal: AI-assisted provisional protocol-completeness review: objectives, allocation, interventions, outcomes, sample-size logic, follow-up and implementation aim are described; the publication contains no trial outcome evidence.
Extração: Protocol plans a 56-participant non-inferiority comparison of BBTI vs CBTI with assessments through 12 months and a CFIR-guided qualitative needs assessment among Veterans and VA staff.
Resultado: Protocol only: no BBTI-versus-CBTI effectiveness, non-inferiority or implementation results can be extracted from this publication.
Localização exata: Abstract—Methods; Methods—Overview and study design; Aim 1; Randomization; Power analysis; Aim 2
Supported claims: The protocol specifies a hybrid type I design combining a randomized non-inferiority insomnia-treatment trial with a CFIR-guided implementation needs assessment.
Unsupported claims: The protocol does not establish that BBTI is non-inferior, improves access, or produces clinical or implementation benefit.
Limites de transferibilidade: Veterans Affairs primary-care delivery, psychotherapy workforce and Veteran population are not direct equivalents of Brazilian police/military public-safety systems.

Título: From benchmarking to best practices: Lessons from the laboratory quality improvement programme at the military teaching hospital in Cotonou, Benin.
Contexto: Cotonou, Benin; Army Teaching Hospital-University Teaching Hospital laboratory
População: Single military teaching-hospital laboratory quality-improvement program, 2015–2018
Desenho: uncontrolled before-after quality-improvement implementation study/program evaluation
Resumo appraisal: AI-assisted provisional JBI quasi-experimental appraisal: intervention sequence and repeated external SLIPTA assessments are described, but no concurrent control exists and attribution to individual program components is limited.
Extração: The laboratory reported a 29 percentage-point increase in SLIPTA score, from 16% at baseline (2015) to 45% at follow-up (2017), alongside quality-management, proficiency-testing, internal-QC and staff-training changes.
Resultado: Observed laboratory quality score improved over time during the QI program; uncontrolled design prevents causal attribution.
Localização exata: Abstract; Intervention; Lessons learnt; Improvement of SLIPTA score; Figure 3; Recommendations
Supported claims: At this Benin military teaching-hospital laboratory, SLIPTA score increased from 16% to 45% during a multi-component quality-improvement program.
Unsupported claims: The study does not prove that any single intervention component caused the improvement or that the same effect would occur in Brazilian tactical/public-safety systems.
Limites de transferibilidade: Military health-system setting is relevant institutionally, but laboratory accreditation, workforce mobility, resources and Benin health governance differ from Brazil.

Título: Comparing the Effects of Low-Dose Ketamine, Fentanyl, and Morphine on Hemorrhagic Tolerance and Analgesia in Humans.
Contexto: United States laboratory; healthy adults; doses derived from TCCC medical guidelines
População: Healthy adults aged 18–45; ketamine n=30, fentanyl n=28, morphine n=30 in separate randomized crossover drug-versus-placebo projects
Desenho: randomized crossover placebo-controlled human experimental studies; between-drug comparison assembled across three cohorts
Versão instrumento: Cochrane RoB 2 current framework; crossover considerations recorded provisionally
Resumo appraisal: AI-assisted provisional RoB 2 domain review: randomized within-drug placebo comparisons and blinding of participants/LBNP stopping assessor are reported; cross-cohort drug comparison and laboratory model constrain direct clinical inference.
Extração: Median hemorrhagic-tolerance CSI as percentage of each placebo trial was ketamine 99 [73–139] (n=30), fentanyl 95 [68–130] (n=28), and morphine 62 [35–85] (n=30); Kruskal-Wallis p=0.002. Morphine was lower than ketamine (post hoc p=0.002) and fentanyl (p=0.02).
Resultado: Morphine reduced tolerance to simulated hemorrhage in the laboratory model relative to its placebo and compared with the other drug cohorts; findings are not direct field-patient outcomes.
Localização exata: Abstract; Methods—Experimental overview/Participants/Protocol/LBNP/Data analysis; Figure 1; Discussion
Supported claims: In healthy adults exposed to a laboratory lower-body-negative-pressure model, the morphine cohort showed lower hemorrhagic tolerance than ketamine and fentanyl cohorts under the reported randomized crossover protocols.
Unsupported claims: The study does not directly establish mortality, shock outcomes, battlefield effectiveness or patient-level superiority of ketamine/fentanyl in actual hemorrhage.
Limites de transferibilidade: TCCC-derived doses increase tactical relevance, but healthy volunteers, simulated hemorrhage, controlled laboratory conditions and U.S. research setting limit operational transfer.

Título: Organizational Capacity for Sexual Assault Prevention Within a U.S. Army Installation.
Contexto: United States; one Army installation; sexual-assault prevention implementation capacity
População: 15 sexual-assault prevention program personnel; individual one-hour semi-structured interviews
Desenho: qualitative implementation-capacity interview study using applied thematic analysis
Resumo appraisal: AI-assisted provisional JBI qualitative appraisal: coherent implementation question, defined personnel sample, semi-structured interviews and applied thematic analysis; one-installation sampling and limited reflexive detail constrain transfer.
Extração: Participants identified proficiencies such as tailoring skills, train-the-trainer capacity and useful existing data, alongside gaps in difficult-conversation facilitation, outcome measurement, leadership investment, trust and informal networking.
Resultado: Findings characterize perceived implementation capacity and organizational gaps; they do not test prevention effectiveness.
Localização exata: Abstract; Materials and Methods; Results; Conclusions
Supported claims: Personnel at one U.S. Army installation identified specific prevention-workforce, data, leadership and collaboration capacities and gaps.
Unsupported claims: The study does not show that the assessed capacities reduce sexual assault incidence or that GTO support will produce improved outcomes.
Limites de transferibilidade: Military organizational relevance is high, but U.S. Army prevention policy, legal environment, program roles and single-installation context differ from Brazilian policing.

Título: Integrating Implementation Science in Interpersonal Violence Research and Practice: A Systematic Review of Barriers and Facilitators of Implementation.
Contexto: United States; healthcare, school, community, correctional and military settings
População: 31 included implementation studies after screening; studies published 2005–2023
Desenho: systematic review with CFIR-based synthesis of implementation barriers and facilitators
Instrumento: JBI Systematic Reviews and Research Syntheses
Resumo appraisal: AI-assisted provisional JBI review appraisal: multi-database search, duplicate screening and transparent criteria are described; synthesis targets implementation determinants rather than intervention effects, and U.S.-only/English peer-reviewed restrictions limit breadth.
Extração: From 1,319 deduplicated records, 31 studies were included. Recurrent barriers included resource/time constraints and leadership issues; facilitators included champions, adaptability, protocols, funding, ongoing training and support.
Resultado: Review synthesizes implementation barriers/facilitators across multiple U.S. settings; it does not estimate pooled effectiveness.
Localização exata: Methods—eligibility/information sources/search/study selection/data extraction; Results—flow and implementation barriers/facilitators; Limitations; Conclusion
Supported claims: Across 31 U.S. implementation studies, the review identified recurring multilevel barriers and facilitators mapped to CFIR domains.
Unsupported claims: The review does not prove that any single implementation strategy causes improved violence outcomes or transfers directly to Brazilian public safety.
Limites de transferibilidade: Includes one military study and varied settings, but the corpus is U.S.-only, English peer-reviewed literature and focused on interpersonal-violence interventions.

Título: Opportunities for the development of drowning interventions in West Bengal, India: a review of policy and government programs.
Contexto: West Bengal, India; policy and government-program implementation environment
População: National/state policy documents and literature on three high-coverage government programs (ICDS, SHG, ASHA)
Desenho: contextual policy content review plus systematic literature review of program reach, barriers, facilitators and equity
Instrumento: JBI Systematic Reviews and Research Syntheses
Resumo appraisal: AI-assisted provisional JBI review appraisal: policy-content analysis is coupled to a systematic literature review, but the question is implementation-oriented and heterogeneity precludes a conventional pooled intervention-effect estimate.
Extração: Three government programs were identified as possible platforms for drowning interventions; reported barriers included weak monitoring, resource limitations and burden on community workers, while program reach and underserved-group coverage were potential facilitators.
Resultado: Contextual implementation opportunities are identified; no drowning-intervention effectiveness was tested.
Localização exata: Abstract; Methods; Results; policy/program tables/figures; Discussion; Conclusions
Supported claims: The review identified three existing West Bengal programs that could potentially support drowning-prevention implementation and documented implementation barriers and equity considerations.
Unsupported claims: The review does not demonstrate that embedding drowning interventions in these programs reduces drowning or will be effective in another jurisdiction.
Limites de transferibilidade: Low- and middle-income implementation constraints may be informative, but India-specific policy, community-worker systems, geography and drowning focus differ sharply from Brazilian public safety.

Título: The intergenerational impact of war on mental health and psychosocial wellbeing: lessons from the longitudinal study of war-affected youth in Sierra Leone.
Contexto: Sierra Leone; fragile post-conflict/humanitarian research setting
População: LSWAY cohort: baseline n=259 war-affected youth aged 10–17; four waves reported (2002, 2004, 2008, 2016/2017) with mixed methods
Desenho: narrative longitudinal-program case study synthesizing methods, findings and implementation lessons from LSWAY
Versão instrumento: SANRA 6-item scale; provisional non-comparative narrative appraisal
Resumo appraisal: AI-assisted provisional SANRA appraisal: rationale, literature linkage, scientific reasoning and program methods are described; article synthesizes a longitudinal research program rather than reporting one new causal estimate.
Extração: LSWAY followed war-affected youth over four waves and used mixed methods to study long-term mental health, social reintegration, parenting and intergenerational patterns; the paper emphasizes field, ethical and implementation challenges in fragile settings.
Resultado: The article supports longitudinal-program and implementation lessons, not a single intervention-effect estimate.
Localização exata: Abstract; Discussion; LSWAY design/method sections; baseline/recruitment description; ethics/field challenges; Conclusion
Supported claims: LSWAY provides a long-term mixed-methods research program on war-affected youth and documents methodological and implementation challenges of longitudinal research in a fragile post-conflict setting.
Unsupported claims: The article does not establish direct applicability to police readiness, nor a causal effect of any single intervention on mental-health or operational outcomes.
Limites de transferibilidade: Trauma and organizational lessons may be conceptually relevant, but former child soldiers, humanitarian systems and Sierra Leone's post-conflict context are far from Brazilian tactical workforce conditions.

Título: Delivering and implementing child and adolescent mental health training for mental health and allied professionals: a systematic review and qualitative meta-aggregation.
Contexto: International evidence; mental-health and allied professionals including police, teachers and youth workers
População: 39 included qualitative studies; 12,448 records initially identified; 182 supported raw findings synthesized
Desenho: systematic review and qualitative meta-aggregation following PRISMA/JBI methods
Instrumento: JBI Systematic Reviews and Research Syntheses
Resumo appraisal: AI-assisted provisional JBI review appraisal: protocol registration, multi-database searching, explicit eligibility, JBI appraisal and meta-aggregation are reported; variation in included-study quality and training contexts limits universal application.
Extração: Thirty-nine studies yielded 182 supported raw findings, condensed into 47 sub-categories, 19 categories and five synthesis statements covering support, content/design/planning, context, perceived value and organizational factors.
Resultado: Review identifies barriers/facilitators to training delivery and workplace implementation; it does not estimate training effectiveness on clinical or operational outcomes.
Localização exata: Abstract; Methods—protocol/eligibility/data synthesis; Results—study selection/synthesised findings; Discussion; Conclusions
Supported claims: Across 39 qualitative studies, the review synthesized five groups of barriers/facilitators relevant to delivery and workplace implementation of child/adolescent mental-health training.
Unsupported claims: The review does not establish that a specific training package improves police performance, clinical outcomes or operational readiness.
Limites de transferibilidade: Some allied-professional evidence includes police, but most included settings/professions are not Brazilian public-safety organizations; implementation must be locally validated.
